title: One matcher round
statement: Let $l,N,j,W$ be natural numbers, and let $pos,neg\in\mathrm{Fin}(l)$ be distinct. Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, let $old,row:\mathrm{Fin}(l)\to\{0,1\}^*$ be rows of Boolean words, and let $target:\mathrm{Fin}(2)\to\{0,1\}^*$ be a pair of target words. For Boolean words $pre,tail$ and a list $flags$ of Boolean values, suppose $j<N$, every word $old(i)$ and $row(i)$ has length at most $W$, and both target words have length at most $W$. Then for some natural number $t\le l(5W+7)+2W+5$, after $t$ steps the matcher is in the configuration with row $row$, stream $pre$ followed by the packed encoding of the fields of $row$ and then $tail$, cursor at the end of that packed encoding, clock position $j+1$, and flags equal to the original list followed by the comparison flag determined by $row$ and $target$ at $pos$ and $neg$.
replaced: For distinct coordinates, old and new candidate rows and target words of field length at most $W$, a stream exposing the packed new row, and a clock position $j < N$, there is a time $t \le l(5W+7) + 2W + 5$ after which the matcher has consumed one clock token, loaded row $j$, compared cross-sums, appended exactly the comparison flag of that row, and advanced its cursor past the row; every reset, stream read, comparison, dispatch, and flag write is included in the bound.
